statement: Combined capex of the 5 largest spenders falls year on year for 2 consecutive quarters (Securities filings; by 2028-06-30)
status_at_phase_end: Outside the resolution window, but the condition pattern occurred in 2023: per the four largest spenders' 10-Q cash-flow lines, combined capex fell year on year in 2023Q1, Q2 and Q3 (a 'capex digestion' cycle at two of them during a construction pause / fulfilment pull-back), while all four guided to higher 2024 capex citing generative AI. Base-rate evidence only - FLAGGED for adjudication on how pre-window occurrences enter replay (direction set toward YES for the decline items).

items.summary: Combined quarterly capex (purchases of property and equipment) of the four largest cloud/AI spenders was lower than a year earlier in three consecutive quarters of 2023: about $33.9 bn vs $35.5 bn (Q1), $33.4 bn vs $37.0 bn (Q2) and $36.9 bn vs $39.3 bn (Q3).
items.detail: Figures summed from Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft 10-Q/10-K cash-flow lines (SEC XBRL), as compiled by ChartedFacts 'Capital expenditure of Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta by quarter' (verified via web_extract this run). The compilation is a later (2026) presentation using latest-filed values; the underlying 2023 Q3 10-Qs were all filed by 2023-10-27 (published date set to the last Q3 filing day, approximate). Fifth-largest spender not included. Not within the 2026-2028 resolution window: base-rate evidence.

items.summary: A top-2 spender reported trailing-12-month capital investments of $54 bn, down from $61 bn a year earlier, and guided full-year 2023 to slightly more than $50 bn vs $59 bn in 2022, with fulfilment and transport capex down, partly offset by cloud infrastructure including generative AI.
items.detail: Amazon Q2 2023 earnings call (CFO Brian Olsavsky), 2023-08-03, transcript via The Motley Fool (verified via web_extract this run).
items.value: $54 bn TTM vs $61 bn; FY2023 guide ~$50 bn vs $59 bn

items.summary: Another top spender's Q3 2023 capex was $6.8 bn vs $9.52 bn a year earlier, attributed to lower server and data-centre construction spend while shifting to a new AI-oriented data-centre design.
items.detail: DatacenterDynamics, 'Meta's CapEx drops almost $3bn during data center construction pause', 2023-10-26 (verified via web_extract this run).

items.summary: Industry analyst: Q3 2023 capex across large web-scale operators was $48.0 bn, the second consecutive ~9% year-on-year decline; all key operators nonetheless expected capex growth ahead, with generative AI an added driver.
items.detail: MTN Consulting (Matt Walker), 'Webscale Network Operators: 3Q23 Market Review', publication date 2023-11-23 (verified via web_extract this run). Broader operator set than the 5 largest; paid report, summary only.

items.summary: A top spender reported a meaningful increase in AI compute investment in Q3 2023 ($8 bn capex) and said 2024 aggregate capex would exceed 2023, signalling the decline phase was ending.
items.detail: Alphabet, 2023 Q3 earnings call, 2023-10-24 (verified via web_extract this run).
